measuredFidelity.note: The rig's 6.75-degree leg splay (render.leg-stance) settled ankle daylight at 48.5% against the concept's 46.9%. Round 7 then found that Junebug's SIGNATURE idle pose carried an 8-degree inward leg roll, authored when the rig ran its legs straight down, which closed the ankles to 0.325ft against the bind pose's 0.756 and failed rubric 3.12 in idle while the bind-pose render this command reads stayed correct. frontProfileSilhouette.label: front/profile silhouette
frontProfileSilhouette.note: Independent 2026-09-24 review of the fresh hand-migration board and runtime evidence. Junebug retains the concept’s bun, headband, swept tail, fitted jersey and knicker silhouette. Measured head height 34.0% versus 33.9%, aspect 0.82 versus 0.84, and ankle daylight 48.5% versus 46.9% all pass. The hair still reads as separate dome, crown and tail forms rather than an organic continuous silhouette; that prevents a 5. No new silhouette regression attributable to the hand migration is visible in the reviewed evidence.

headBodyProportions.label: head/body proportions
headBodyProportions.note: Fresh measure:fidelity passes all nine metrics. Child proportions remain those of the approved turnaround, with knees bending and separated legs in the sampled run frames. At 4x crops of bat_stance-0-0 and bat_stance-0-1, wrists remain continuous, elbow bends face the expected directions, and four slender fingers visibly curl around the bat. No detached digit, reverse elbow or torso penetration is apparent in the supplied run, throw and upset samples. This is sampled pose evidence, not a certification of all transitions or every possible clip angle. The shared bunt receiving pose at 0.67s still raises the handle-side elbow beside the face and makes its forearm nearly vertical; the hand rig itself remains connected.

hairMass.label: hair mass
hairMass.note: The fresh runtime hero and board show a clean hairline with no bare-skull read, but the smooth bun, crown and bulb-ended tail still read as assembled masses. Source inspection confirms the hair tie is built as a capped tube on the tail axis (build_hair area around lines 2280-2313), not an absent feature or literally a single quad; its extent still reads as a broad tab in this gameplay view. Judged its geometry, not its raw grey/yellow TEAM_MASK colour. Historical strand-count and notch alpha measurements were not rerun for this scoped hand migration and are preserved as historical findings only. Current visible mass construction remains below the rubric’s coherent designed-mass 4 bar.

clothingConstruction.label: clothing construction
clothingConstruction.note: The fresh board and runtime hero retain visible V-neck piping, placket buttons, sleeve stripes and cuffs, belt, sock bands, shoe soles and raised laces. Those constructed details survive the migrated arm poses; no new sleeve tear or hand-to-cuff gap is visible. The jersey/pelvis junction still has an abrupt straight ledge and the laces read as straps rather than woven lacing, keeping this at 4. Historical exact pixel crops were not remeasured.

faceExpressionRead.label: face/expression read
faceExpressionRead.note: Fresh hero and all four runtime expression stills were inspected. Eyes, sclera, brows, nose, ears and the open smiling mouths remain readable. Grin, cheer and tongue still look nearly identical at draft-card scale, while angry is distinct; no claim of a fresh numerical mouth-diff is made. Neutral remains a very small mouth. These limitations keep the expressive range at 4; the hand migration has not visibly damaged the face.

heroAndFieldScale.label: hero + 40px read
heroAndFieldScale.note: Fresh runtime hero explicitly reports model model. Junebug’s headband/bun, strong brows, red uniform and pale shoes read clearly at hero scale and in the board’s 40-pixel strip. Her upgraded fingers are visible at hero scale without changing the character identity. The frontal 40-pixel read does not carry the tail well, and the tail tie is still visually broad at hero scale, so this stays 4. Technical grip checks do not substitute for whole-character approval.
